While the spotlight this week was stolen by the iOS 27 public beta, Apple has simultaneously rolled out a new public beta firmware update for AirPods. This update brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods Public Beta Details

The AirPods public beta firmware version is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models are eligible for this update:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 (Active Noise Cancellation)
  • AirPods Max 2

You can join the AirPods Public Beta programme within the "Settings" app on your iPhone. After connecting your AirPods, you'll see a toggle in the "Settings" app to enable the beta firmware. Thereafter, as long as your AirPods are in their charging case and within range of the paired iPhone, the beta will download and install automatically.

  • Open the "Settings" app
  • Tap "Bluetooth"
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and enable the "AirPods Beta Updates" option

Custom EQ Lands on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, you'll find a long-awaited new feature in the "Settings" app: custom EQ.

Thanks to the newly added custom EQ controls, you can now fine-tune the sound of your AirPods with greater flexibility. Within the "Settings" app, you can adjust the bass, mid, and treble performance of your AirPods.

Apple explains on its website: "AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully reproduce audio exactly as intended—whether it's music, TV shows, films, or calls. If you prefer a different sound signature, you can also customise the audio output of your AirPods across all types of content."

While adjusting custom EQ, you can play songs from Apple Music directly within the "Settings" app to hear the changes in real time.

This is hardly the most advanced equaliser out there—merely a basic three-band system. But for AirPods users, this has been a long time coming, and Apple has finally delivered—although most users will probably stick with the default settings.

You can find this new custom EQ feature under "Audio & Routing" within the AirPods menu in the "Settings" app. All AirPods equipped with the H2 chip support this feature, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other New Features iOS 27 Brings to AirPods

Here's a look at other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned "Settings" app interface: In iOS 27, Apple has redesigned the AirPods interface within the "Settings" app. The controls have been reorganised, categorising features such as Hearing Health, Find My, and Live Translation.
  • Adaptive Audio slider: The "Settings" app now includes a slider for more granular adjustment of Adaptive Audio mode.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for years, it has always required pairing with an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac noted, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to the iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding via the "Find My" app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a compatible iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrap-Up

Which new AirPods feature are you most eager to try? Will you experiment with the new custom EQ? Let us know in the comments.
